column1: # What each RELEASED version of day does when handed the block shapes this
# commit writes. One row per tag; the tag being released is excluded, since a
# version cannot be a historical reader of its own release.
# These are CHARACTERIZATIONS, not correctness assertions. A released binary
# cannot be fixed, so the matrix's job is to make the blast radius of a
# block-shape change visible *before* it ships rather than after, which is the
# thing day#78 needed and did not have.
# Outcomes:
#   refused-honestly   said it could not read the block
#   silently-widened   loaded it as though the unreadable part were absent, and
#                      certified the result -- day#78's shape
#   unbuildable        does not build with the current toolchain, so nobody is
#                      running it
#   errored            failed some other way
# Every version below predates the `_version` gate, so every one of them
# silently widens. That is not a list of bugs to fix -- it is day#78's residue,
# quantified. `v0.7.0-beta.2` is the first version that will read
# `refused-honestly`, and it will appear here as a row the release after it.
# Changing a block shape and changing a row below belong in the SAME commit. A
# row that moved on its own is the matrix telling you something you did not
# intend.
# tag
